The HKMA is committed to reducing the carbon footprint of its own organisation, with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and contributing to Hong Kong's overall climate goals. On one hand, the HKMA works hard to promote environmental sustainability, while on the other hand, it fulfils its commitments to caring for the physical and mental well-being of its staff, encouraging financial inclusion, and discharging its social responsibilities. The HKMA is dedicated to conducting its day-to-day operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA puts sustainability into practice under the three pillars of environment, staff and social responsibility (Figure 1). The Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating and implementing its sustainability strategy. The Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with members including three Deputy Chief Executives, as well as representatives from the Risk Management and Compliance Department and the Corporate Development and Operations Department; and it submits regular reports to the Governance Sub-Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the leadership of the Committee, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing measures within their respective areas. In 2022, the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved the climate targets for corporate operations and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the Committee continued to review the HKMA's progress on green measures, including recommendations to strengthen the HKMA's sustainable procurement policies, procedures and methodologies.  Sustainability Governance Structure  The HKMA's Corporate Sustainability Journey  In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for the 16th consecutive year. The HKMA pays great attention to the carbon footprint of its own organisation and has established a set of internal "Green Office Guidelines" to manage and control the environmental impact of its operational procedures. The HKMA has integrated environmental considerations into the interior design, operation and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus awarded the HKMA a Gold certification for certain renovated office areas. This is the second green building certification obtained following the LEED Gold certification received in 2021. Awarded BEAM Plus Interior Version 1.0 Gold The HKMA has implemented a number of energy-saving measures. In 2022, total energy consumption was 4,996.4 megawatt-hours (2.8 megawatt-hours per person), a decrease of 24.4% compared with 2015 (Figure 1). In 2022, total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions were 2,996.4 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per person), a reduction of 38.2% compared with 2015 (Figure 2). Figure 1 Figure 2 Greenhouse Gas Emissions Intensity (Scope 1 and 2) The HKMA encourages paperless operations within the organisation. In addition, the HKMA has implemented a print management system whereby staff must log in at the printer to confirm each print request, helping to reduce unnecessary printouts and toner usage. Where printing is genuinely necessary, double-sided printing and black-and-white printing are also encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic records-keeping system. In 2022, total paper consumption was 20.5 tonnes (0.0114 tonnes per person), a reduction of 65.3% compared with 2015 (Figure A). Figure A: Paper Intensity The HKMA continues to adhere to the "4R" principle in its waste management work. In addition to conventional waste, the HKMA also reduces electronic waste by adopting technological solutions such as server virtualisation and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to analyse the composition of waste generated by the office. The audit found that food waste accounted for a large portion of the total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling programme (see "Enhancing Waste Management" on page 41). In 2022, the total amount of non-hazardous waste generated (including general refuse and recyclable waste) was 242.0 tonnes (0.135 tonnes per person), a reduction of 4.8% compared with 2015 (Figure 3). The fluctuating trend was mainly due to the work-from-home arrangements implemented during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resumption of office operations after the fifth wave of the pandemic. Figure 3 Non-Hazardous Waste Intensity The HKMA gives priority to waste reduction at source and is committed to reducing, reusing and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to gain a clearer understanding of the composition of waste in its day-to-day operations (plastics, paper, metal, glass, wood, electronics, etc.) and to provide waste reduction recommendations. Based on the results of this audit, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, setting up food waste collection bins in all pantries. The food waste collected each day is transported to an organic resources recovery centre in Hong Kong, where it is converted into renewable energy to generate electricity. The residues produced during the conversion process can also be made into compost for use in landscaping and agricultural production. In addition, recycling bins are set up at various locations in the office for convenient use. The HKMA shares recycling tips with staff and pays greater attention to further improving the source separation of recyclables, as well as the points to note when handling recyclable items such as cardboard boxes, food containers and beverage bottles. In addition, we continue to organise activities to raise staff's environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage staff to make good use of the recycling facilities in the office. Food waste collected each day is transported to the organic resources recovery centre Recycled plastic items The HKMA operates two data centres (a primary one and a backup one). As both account for a major portion of the organisation's overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green designs and a number of energy-saving measures, including cabinet-type air-conditioning systems, LED lighting equipment and round-the-clock monitoring of energy efficiency. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of the above data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations for enhancing overall energy efficiency. It has also begun preparations to obtain green data centre certification. The HKMA understands the importance of building a culture of sustainability and therefore regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to develop habits conducive to sustainability and to adopt green and digital ways of working. The HKMA shares green living tips with staff, along with office-wide annual energy and paper consumption statistics, to remind them to help address environmental matters at the individual level; staff are also encouraged to put forward suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by senior managers of the Administration Division, a focus group brings together staff from different departments to brainstorm and put forward ideas and specific measures to promote a green working environment. Members of the focus group also serve as ambassadors when new green measures are rolled out. The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly working practices and has launched a number of measures to improve the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry and the economy as a whole, while minimising the consumption of resources. The HKMA's Submission Through Electronic Transmission (STET) system is a one-stop platform that allows banks to submit documents to the HKMA electronically, covering various types of periodic returns required to be submitted on a weekly, monthly, quarterly or annual basis. Another system, e-Delivery, is a secure electronic communication channel that allows the HKMA to issue information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. Both systems help save a substantial amount of paper each year. In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless submission of documents, and bank customers can lodge complaints through electronic channels and by completing online forms. The HKMA is also developing a next-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper usage, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) has adopted digital signatures in its day-to-day communications with participants, including the issuance of circulars, account opening and account termination letters, as well as responses to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore more green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic procedures for internal and external communications. The HKMA encourages the public to make greater use of electronic payment methods in place of cash and physical cheques by promoting the use of the Faster Payment System ("FPS") and stored value facilities. Further information on the FPS and stored value facilities is set out in the chapter "Hong Kong as an International Financial Centre" of the HKMA Annual Report 2022. Distributing electronic lai see is simple and convenient, and it reduces the use of physical red packets and banknotes, helping to promote sustainability in Hong Kong. To this end, the HKMA continued to actively promote on various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to distribute electronic lai see through online or mobile banking services using FPS or other e-wallet services during the Lunar New Year. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organised various activities to attract users to use electronic lai see, such as offering festive-themed user interfaces, enhancing functions to make usage more convenient, and launching lucky draws or cash rebates. The HKMA promotes electronic lai see on social media platforms For members of the public who choose to distribute physical lai see during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continued to encourage them to use "good-as-new notes"—that is, banknotes that, though used, remain crisp and clean—for packing lai see. Good-as-new notes can reduce the need to print new banknotes, thereby reducing the environmental impact. Feedback from note-issuing banks indicates that the public has become increasingly receptive to good-as-new notes in recent years. The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA's efforts in promoting the recycling of coins. Coins collected through the programme are returned to the market to meet public demand, enhancing the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for minting. The programme operates two Coin Carts, which to date have served the public over 1 million times and collected more than 800 million coins with a total face value of about HK$1.3 billion. In 2022, about 78% of users chose to use part or all of the value of their coins to top up their stored value facility accounts. The HKMA has maintained cooperation with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying Coin Carts to collect coins on flag days of non-governmental organisations, in an effort to support social services. Coin-counting machines on the Coin Cart The Coin Collection Programme was launched in 2014 and was the first systematic coin collection programme in the world to adopt the mobile-vehicle concept. Over the years, it has received a number of local and international awards, with its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to handling coins widely recognised. The programme operates two Coin Carts, each equipped with two high-speed coin-counting machines, to collect coins exchanged by members of the public. Members of the public can choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, use them to top up stored value facility (such as Octopus cards or e-wallets) accounts, or donate them to the Community Chest for charity. In addition to collecting coins, the Coin Carts are also deployed from time to time for various educational activities (such as student visits).

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the climate targets ("Climate Targets") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Climate Targets were established with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual (the "SBTi Corporate Manual"). The purpose of this verification exercise was to verify whether the Climate Targets were established with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. This verification exercise was carried out in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion so as to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA was responsible for the collection and presentation of the data. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets were established with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Shen Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023.  Verification Statement  The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the 2022 environmental data (the "2022 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The 2022 Data includes the total energy consumption for 2022, the intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption intensity, the intensity and recycling rate of non-hazardous waste generated, as well as the changes in these figures compared with 2015 levels. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data was prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute ("WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development ("WBCSD"). The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, and also covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison. The scope of verification encompassed a total of 6 office and warehouse assets: 4 offices located at 1) the office at Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre; and 2 warehouses at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre and 6) Sung Lee Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification exercise was carried out in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion so as to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to its source, and also reviewed the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking, and conducted reliability testing. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA was responsible for the collection and presentation of the data. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the preparation process of the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance regarding the 2022 Data and concludes that: • The 2022 Data is substantially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shen Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023.

Scaling up and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing issue of our time. We are almost halfway through the critical decade for the climate crisis. We need to cut global carbon emissions by more than 40% within this decade in order to have any hope of limiting global warming to within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Yet, greenhouse gas emissions keep hitting record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window for limiting the rise in global temperature to within 1.5 degrees Celsius is fast closing. The impact of the 1.1 degrees Celsius temperature rise is already being felt clearly by everyone — record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding, storms and other extreme weather events are occurring more frequently across the globe, and each one more severe than the last. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, following the assault of a powerful super typhoon, we were immediately hit by a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our robust infrastructure and swift disaster response capabilities, the impact was still very severe — widespread flooding, disrupted traffic, and damaged roads in numerous locations. All of this serves as a clear reminder that decisive and proactive climate action is truly a matter of urgency.  Asia faces particularly significant challenges on the path to low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Owing to the region's rapid economic development and fast-growing population, its carbon emissions account for more than half of global total emissions. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region is highly densely populated and, due to its geographical location, is also vulnerable to rising sea levels and extreme weather. As the economies in the region are at different stages of development, while the low-carbon transition will bring new opportunities to some economies, for others, raising the funds needed for transition poses an enormous challenge. The market estimates that the Asia-Pacific region will require more than US$3 trillion in low-carbon transition investment annually over the next 30 years.  As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the ability and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across Asia. As a banking regulator, market facilitator and responsible investor, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been making substantial efforts on the sustainability agenda. Readers will be able to learn from the various chapters of this report about the specific measures and work introduced by the HKMA over the past year. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA's internal governance structure and to more effectively coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee last year. For detailed information about the Steering Committee, please refer to the newly added chapter "Governance for Sustainability".  Hong Kong banks play an important role in supporting Asia's transition to net-zero emissions. In addition to fulfilling the traditional functions of a banking regulator — ensuring that banks properly manage climate risks in our day-to-day supervisory work — we also play the role of a facilitator, supporting the banking sector in financing the low-carbon transition. One such example is the development of a green taxonomy framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched the prototype of the green taxonomy framework for consultation in May, and are now refining the framework based on the feedback gathered during the consultation period. In addition, as there is growing demand across all sectors for higher-quality and more globally comparable sustainability disclosure information, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards launched by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June — a comprehensive global baseline for common sustainability reporting.  The HKMA's role as a facilitator is not limited to formulating frameworks and rules; we are also committed to resolving the pain points faced by the industry. At present, many banks are constrained by data limitations, making it difficult to conduct physical risk assessments. In view of this, the HKMA will soon launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform whereby banks need only enter a property address to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby helping banks manage the related climate risks.  As Asia's leading international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has long served as a bridge, channelling international investment towards sustainable development projects in Asia and supporting the region's low-carbon transition. In recent years, the total amount of international green and sustainable bonds arranged for issuance in Hong Kong has accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, clearly leading other regions. It is particularly worth mentioning that the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong in 2023 for the third and second consecutive year respectively, once again affirming Hong Kong's important role as the green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world.  The flourishing of Hong Kong's sustainable bond activities is partly attributable to the demonstration effect of the "Government Green Bond Programme". Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds with a total value of about US$25 billion, sold to institutional and retail investors. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds — including currency denominations, tenors and distribution channels — laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bond in 2022, we issued the world's first batch of tokenised government green bonds in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the second batch of tokenised green bond issuance; these bonds were denominated in four major currencies and issued in digitally native form, making them the world's first multi-currency digital green bonds.  At the same time, we have also proactively introduced a range of measures to enhance the vitality and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. This covers work in various areas including skills training, data improvement, green fintech and transition finance. In particular, in terms of talent development, in 2023 we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the banking professional qualifications framework, providing banking practitioners with systematic courses to enhance their understanding of and professional knowledge in green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key area of our work; it provides funding for the decarbonisation activities of high-carbon-emitting and hard-to-abate industries, preventing such industries from being unable to transition due to a lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong's green taxonomy framework to cover transition activities. We will also expand the coverage of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme", which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, so as to encourage enterprises in the region to raise transition funds in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders, and through public-private partnerships and blended finance models, attract private enterprises to invest in sustainable development projects that have previously found it difficult to obtain financing.  Some of the work mentioned above requires cross-sectoral collaboration, and is mainly coordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, which is co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-standing cooperation with the International Finance Corporation on the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks", the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office also joined the "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" and the "Partnership for Green Development Investment and Financing" in 2023 as a founding member. In addition, the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero" has also announced plans to set up a chapter in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we hope to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, and in turn support the channelling of funds towards sustainable development projects in the region and around the world.  To drive new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped host the inaugural "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including top decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to jointly discuss solutions for scaling up climate finance in the region and to forge new partnerships in this regard. Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivered a speech at the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum", the flagship event of "Hong Kong Green Week".  As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a major global asset owner, the HKMA leads by example in being a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of green and sustainable asset investment, and has gradually expanded the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset portfolios in both public and private markets. In relation to the target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's Investment Portfolio by 2050 or before, last year the HKMA added a new actively managed global equity portfolio themed on sustainability and climate transition, while also extending the application of the customised low-carbon equity index to another public market asset portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds that the HKMA prioritises for investment have outperformed the investment benchmark, embodying the proposition of "doing good while doing well". In the private markets, we continued to pursue green-related investment opportunities, and became an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio decreased by 6% and 46% compared with 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently remained below the overall market level.  As a sustainable organisation, the HKMA will continue to strive for progress, formulating our sustainability goals and plans based on the three pillars of the environment, employees and social responsibility. Specifically, on the HKMA's low-carbon transition journey, we continue to strengthen our capacity to respond to climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emissions reduction, improving energy efficiency and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have already formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the short term, and have made good progress towards the interim target of Scope 2 emissions reduction by 2030. To attract and retain top talent to carry out the HKMA's various important functions, in addition to our green goals, the HKMA is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our staff. Furthermore, by working with various stakeholders, we contribute to building a caring society through promoting financial inclusion, enhancing the public's level of financial literacy, and raising public awareness of guarding against financial fraud.  The climate challenge is immense and exceptionally urgent. Economies around the world are moving towards a more sustainable future, a process that is expected to bring about tremendous changes in financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries considerable risks, but will also be accompanied by unprecedented opportunities. As a major global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has the responsibility to take the lead in action to address these challenges. At the same time, we are also well positioned to ride this momentum. The HKMA will fully support the industry in financing the low-carbon transition; and will continue to be a responsible investor and a sustainable organisation, leading by example and working with like-minded partners to advance this global agenda that is of the utmost importance at present.  Chief Executive Eddie Yue

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are of global concern. The HKMA's goal in its sustainability work is to strive to play a leading role through its own policies and operations, ensuring that Hong Kong's financial system and the HKMA itself can withstand the risks of climate change, and to support the transition to more sustainable economic development. Through active participation in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also strive to contribute to the development of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both the regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking industry's climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, the key priorities include: launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting a new round of consultation sessions as part of assessing banks' progress in implementing the supervisory requirements on climate risk management; continuing the work of incorporating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; completing the second round of the industry-wide climate risk stress test, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing the observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including working with relevant local authorities to keep the relevant requirements aligned with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Pillar 3¹ framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing with the industry guidance on best practices for transition planning. To promote the healthy development of banks in offering green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to keep abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments, and maintain contact with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate selling processes. In addition, the HKMA will also play the role of a facilitator, striving to promote the development of the green finance ecosystem and to support banks in providing financing for economic transition. We will soon publish the local green taxonomy and continue to expand its coverage to include more activities such as transition activities. At the same time, we will also continue to explore the application of technology solutions to help banks identify, measure and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the upcoming cloud-based platform, which will facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance practitioners' professional capabilities, in 2024 we will also develop the Professional Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners". Hong Kong is well positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposals in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope covered by the "Government Green Bond Programme" to sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market; at the same time, through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme", it aims to attract more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions and enterprises to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and explore the potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to assist in implementing the government-funded "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme" to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. As co-chairs of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group" (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and work relating to promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus its work on three areas, including sustainability disclosure, the application of technology and transition finance. As another key area of work, through the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks", the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various dedicated programmes in the Asian region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training to banks, and providing practical guidance to help banks support financial institutions in developing their tailored green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our cooperation with the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero", the "Coalition for Climate Resilient Investment" and the "Green Investment and Financing Partnership". As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving the net-zero emissions target for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring that the resilience of the asset portfolio is maintained on the path towards net zero. We are well aware that achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a whole-of-economy transition, and therefore we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus, while taking into account the Exchange Fund's investment objectives, on assets that can bring positive climate benefits to the real economy. As an environmentally conscious institution, the HKMA's decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest market, regulatory, technological and other climate-related developments. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff to participate in our sustainability work, including launching awareness campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and optimising office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices when selecting and renewing contracts. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the designated certification standards. As regards the regular upgrades of the data centre facilities, in addition to keeping abreast of the latest technological developments, we will also incorporate green design and practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and actively modernise our internal systems to enhance efficiency and minimise potential risks as far as possible. Finally, in terms of the social focus area, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for our colleagues, and work with the industry to promote financial inclusion and financial literacy, as well as to raise public awareness of guarding against financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to reducing its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, a banking regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor and a sustainable development institution, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the entire Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework that leads the formulation of the HKMA's relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of relevant measures, and ensures that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working methods. In its commitment to practising good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust governance framework for its sustainability-related work, featuring clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainability work. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for monitoring the HKMA's work, including its work on sustainability, and for making recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; in respect of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and in respect of other functional areas, the relevant teams and working groups responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), jointly initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders, in order to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability initiatives over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a brand-new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all of the HKMA's sustainability work across its different functional areas.¹ The Steering Committee provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; assesses the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees the external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. In addition, we will invite the Assistant Chief Executives responsible for the key functions related to green and sustainability matters to attend the Steering Committee meetings to report on the major achievements of their work and their future plans. The Steering Committee holds meetings regularly, and is supported by the relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Department and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC jointly initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020.² As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts on the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, so as to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations. To continue to fulfil their important functions in the financial system and to channel more funding towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the regulator of the banking industry, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks' capabilities to respond to and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is dedicated to formulating various policy measures to strengthen the banking system's capability to respond to climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness during the economic transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of that circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey of selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices relating to transition planning with the industry, and will organise seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experience across the industry. On the disclosure requirements front, in response to the latest international developments—including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June and the consultation launched by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) in November on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks—the HKMA is stepping up its work to enhance the sustainability-related disclosure framework for banks in Hong Kong. Specifically, the HKMA is working with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that aligns with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to banks to help them further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk considerations into banking supervisory processes. Climate risk management has now become a standing agenda item at prudential supervisory meetings held with banks' management. Banking supervisors have also adopted an enhanced CAMEL rating system¹ that incorporates climate risk considerations to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk considerations into banking supervisory processes, the HKMA revised the "greenness" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, in order to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks in responding to climate risks. Regarding the key work priorities under the two-year plan in 2023, following the end of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management", the HKMA launched a round of thematic examinations on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic examination covered four major areas, including the governance structure for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategies, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made a number of enhancements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including introducing a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of economic and climate change shocks occurring simultaneously. Following these enhancements, and as part of the HKMA's regular supervisor-led stress testing programme, the second round of the climate risk stress test was launched in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and to further enhance banks' capabilities in managing climate risks. A total of 44 banks participated in this risk stress test, representing an increase of more than 60% compared with the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also held a climate risk stress test forum in November, which was attended by as many as 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the sharing of experience among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The HKMA held meetings with banks' management to discuss their work on climate risk management and the common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other publicly available information to assess their progress in this regard. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations. As global attention to climate change grows and efforts to address the issue intensify, the HKMA has noted an increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering related products to meet customer needs. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' selling of green and sustainable investment products and, in November, issued a circular setting out the standards the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing the good practices observed. The circular covered a number of areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training and record-keeping, with the aim of reducing potential greenwashing risks and strengthening investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of the relevant investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analytics, thereby strengthening banks' capabilities in managing climate risks. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot version of a cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to work with other central banks and regulators to explore how technological solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. On another front, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) approaches through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, so as to reduce the compliance-related resources consumed. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby enhancing banks' workflows for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA held the "Green Fintech Competition", which aimed to seek market-ready solutions to help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted more than 85 submissions from around 70 companies. In December, the HKMA held the "Green and Sustainable Banking Conference", providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the role of low-carbon technology and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and on the Mainland, and announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition" at the same event. This event attracted around 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and to make green and sustainable financing decisions more consistent, the HKMA, with the assistance of a consultancy firm, developed a local green classification framework. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype of a Green Classification Framework for Hong Kong", inviting stakeholders' views on establishing and implementing a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying other areas for the next phase of the framework's development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has recognised environmental crimes as predicate offences for money laundering; in view of the interconnection between AML and environmental, social and governance (ESG) matters, this area is receiving increasing attention from regulators. The HKMA is keenly aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing monitoring work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, and has included analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the transition planning working group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analysing the interplay between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to develop a forward-looking and dynamic perspective in examining climate-related financial risks. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial industry and the economy. Research topics included the climate risk exposures of the banking industry and investment funds², ESG fund flows³, the impact of climate change on property prices⁴, and the ripple effects of corporates' ESG performance in global supply chains⁵. The findings of the above research have enhanced the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, aiding the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, this research helps strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares its research findings with a wide range of stakeholders through international activities on climate-related matters and various channels such as the HKMA Research Memoranda. The HKMA's Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralised standby liquidity arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. In line with the NGFS's recommendations, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on responding to climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, the HKMA helps foster international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights from it to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to jointly build a richer ecosystem and drive the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial industry's responses to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategy. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing sustainable finance opportunities, with major areas of work including sustainability disclosure, strengthening the ecosystem, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Working Group on Sustainability Disclosure has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover four key areas, including sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Working Group on Transition Finance has also been established to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in conducting transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group has also strengthened the building of the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. In particular, on the data front, we continued to promote the adoption of the climate and environmental risk questionnaire² for unlisted companies that the Steering Group launched in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to stay abreast of the latest developments in the green and sustainable finance field and enhance Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region and globally. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new major workstreams to seize the investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To facilitate industry skills training, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government's Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which provides subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates who receive green and sustainable finance-related training and obtain relevant qualifications. As at December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications had been registered as eligible training or qualifications under the scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications had been approved. The HKMA also launched a new module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" at the foundational level under the "Enhanced Competency Framework". This module aims to promote talent development in the banking industry and enhance the overall professional capabilities of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking industry to develop the professional level of this module to meet the rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals in the industry. To help financial institutions and corporates, particularly SMEs, better understand key climate and sustainability-related topics, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning, during the year the HKMA co-organised a series of seminars and thematic workshops with relevant policy bureaux and departments of the Government, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)³, and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF)⁴, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. On the student front, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Initiative" in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns' and university bachelor's degree graduates' understanding of sustainable finance. The HKMA is well aware of the potential of technology to fill climate-related data gaps and improve data quality, and is therefore committed to making relevant data more accessible and enhancing data quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancement measures to provide financial institutions, corporates, and the public with one-stop green and sustainable finance information. Key enhancements included a sustainability disclosure e-platform, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralised, easily accessible, and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week", the Steering Group also co-organised the "Harnessing Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance" event with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong to showcase leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week — Finance Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia, and consultancy firms. The highlight event of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum" co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together more than 400 guests, including top decision-makers from the global business and finance sectors, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. This two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industries, the circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in the emerging and developing markets of the Asia-Pacific region. The forum received support from public and private sector organisations, which co-organised more than 10 roundtables, seminars, and other exchange activities. The topics covered climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomy, and green development financing in the "Belt and Road" regions. In addition, the HKMA co-organised the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" with the International Monetary Fund on 29 February 2024 to explore key measures to scale up climate finance and the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. The above events form part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as a useful platform to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks"⁵ as a collaboration platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry organisations, research institutions, and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held a total of 22 training events and roundtables, attracting more than 7,300 participants from across the globe, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, together with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second frontier research report titled "Developing an Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategy: Case Studies". During the year, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" (CASI) and the "Green Investment and Finance Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition. The collaboration with CASI and GIFP will help facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more funding towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and the wider region. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong chapter to help support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and the Mainland. The HKMA supports GFANZ's work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. The HKMA assists in the issuance of green bonds under the Programme. To date, the Government has issued about US$25 billion equivalent of green institutional and retail bonds, with the proceeds allocated to more than 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Programme, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report" detailing the allocation of proceeds from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. In the 2023–24 financial year, the Government continued its regular green institutional bond issuance work and issued about US$6 billion equivalent of green bonds in June. This triple-currency issuance covered US dollar, euro, and renminbi bonds of different tenors, attracting a diverse range of investors with an enthusiastic subscription response, recording subscriptions of nearly US$30 billion equivalent. Among them, the issuance size of the renminbi bonds increased from RMB10 billion issued in January to RMB15 billion, and a 10-year renminbi bond was added for the first time, helping to extend the Government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich the range of offshore renminbi products. The enthusiastic response of global investors to the Government's green bond issuance reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued a second batch of green retail bonds with a total value of HK$20 billion, further promoting market development and advancing financial inclusion. This issuance provided members of the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, allowing them to both participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) plays a pivotal role in promoting the development of green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been leading the way in green and sustainable asset investment, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership and to integrate environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "Capital Preservation First, Long-term Value Enhancement", believing that giving full consideration to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps reduce related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and to set a "Net Zero by 2050" target for its investment portfolio, the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasising sustainability—particularly the pressing issue of climate change—with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and striving for more favourable risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practices and standards, and promoting the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and the central banking community. Through stewardship and collaborative measures, the HKMA is dedicated to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand.  Figure 1: The Exchange Fund's Responsible Investment Journey  Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is essential for integrating sustainability and for planning a credible climate transition to achieve net zero targets. To fulfil its commitments in support of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example by compiling this chapter on the Exchange Fund's responsible investment in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The foremost guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Sub-Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Sub-Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors the relevant implementation through regular reporting from the Sustainable Investing Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, convenes semi-annually to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures across the various functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives.  Figure 2: The Responsible Investment Governance Structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office  As shown in Figure 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, with the initial focus on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainable development evolved rapidly and moved beyond risk considerations to become a priority strategic focus for major institutions around the world, the Exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, when the Exchange Fund Investment Office established a new Business Strategy Division led by the Chief Strategy Officer, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, and incorporating the dedicated responsible investment team—now known as the Sustainable Investing Team—which was previously under the Risk Management and Compliance Division. This strategic move reflects the HKMA's shift in the focus of responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainable development-related matters in investment. The Sustainable Investing Team works closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors, and assists senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG—particularly climate-related—risks and opportunities across various types of investments:  Public Market Investments — The Credit, Compliance and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the input of the Sustainable Investing Team, and monitors the ESG status of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting from the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investing Team also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring processes of external investment managers for equity portfolios (see the section "Promoting Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" under the "Risk Management" part on page 40 for details).  Private Market Investments — The Investment Sub-Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams on each investment proposal.  The HKMA understands that the physical and transition risks brought about by climate change, as well as related opportunities, will affect the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investments. The Emissions Gap Report 2023 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced around the world, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The pressing need for more aggressive policies, technological development or behavioural changes to curb temperature rise may exacerbate transition risks such as asset depreciation or stranded asset shocks. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and severe, posing additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG considerations. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 or before, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged efforts, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The approaches concerned are detailed in the following sections. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the primary investment objective of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess outstanding technology and good corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding or divesting from related investments does nothing to solve the carbon emissions problem. On the contrary, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, driving them to implement a transition to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about beneficial changes both for themselves and for the world at large. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net zero investment strategy, adopting a comprehensive approach to pursue transition outcomes that align with the Exchange Fund's and the global net zero targets, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment.
