The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organisation, adopting a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also places emphasis on the health and well-being of its staff and its social responsibility, and strives to advance financial inclusion as well as enhance the public's financial literacy. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA has set sustainability targets under three pillars, namely the environment, staff, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for the various organisational sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee was formerly known as the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, and is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategies, and policies on organisational sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Task Force provide support in coordinating the organisation's sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform to discuss how to create a green working environment and to pool ideas, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of participating in volunteer activities. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transformation. The focus of the work is to implement decarbonisation strategies in its daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green commuting, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools, and more environmentally friendly modes of operation, reducing waste, and building a culture of sustainability. The HKMA also plans to apply carbon-embedded tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, while adopting carbon offset measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. Apart from the aforementioned environmental commitments relating to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to roll out more environmentally friendly operational solutions for the wider community, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and make contact, as well as electronic payment and coin collection programmes for the general public. To enhance and sustain its operational capabilities, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and places emphasis on the health and well-being of its staff. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages staff to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers engaging social enterprises (SEs) in procurement; promotes consumer education on financial services; and works with the banking industry to ensure that all sectors of society can gain fair access to basic banking services. The remainder of this chapter sets out the details of the various strategies mentioned above. Under the HKMA's overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats the HKMA faces in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts brought about by climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more extreme weather, may affect the HKMA's offices and hinder staff travel. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plans to cope with extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also regularly conducts evacuation and back-up facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. Various measures have also been incorporated into the design of the offices to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel, and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions for Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) across all areas of its organisational operations by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and, using 2015 as the base year, to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various decarbonisation and offset strategies. Despite the challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will nonetheless adopt a multi-pronged approach, to the extent practicable, to minimise Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions (such as paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were formulated with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which has also been validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste data disclosed in this report. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the Annual Report 2022, the HKMA also independently published its Sustainability Report 2022 for the first time. The HKMA's efforts to enhance ESG reporting were recognised, winning the ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulator to win an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for meeting good ESG standards, noting that the Sustainability Report is clear and easy to read, and that the appointment of an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to highly transparent and accountable reporting. In addition, the HKMA received the highest rating—the Gold Award in the "Non-profit-making and Charitable Organisations" category—in the Hong Kong Management Association's "Best Annual Reports Awards 2023". The judging panel praised the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's determination to enhance financial literacy and promote financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impacts arising from its operations, and its internal Green Office Guidelines provide staff with guidance on resource use and the generation of office waste. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of the offices it owns and leases. When renovating offices, existing furniture and fitting-out materials are reused as far as possible to reduce waste, and priority is given to environmentally friendly building and decorative materials. The HKMA has consistently adopted this practice, and as a result, in 2021 and 2022 respectively, some of the offices it had completed renovating at Two International Finance Centre were awarded Gold certification under LEED and BEAM Plus Interiors. Improving energy efficiency through the adoption of new technologies and the effective use of existing technologies remains one of the HKMA's key areas of focus. In addition to promoting good habits, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in the work area outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include using light-emitting diode (LED) lighting fixtures and motion sensors, setting the air-conditioning room temperature at an appropriate level, and making effective use of energy in the IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has continued to decrease, standing at 2.59 megawatt-hours per person in 2023, a decrease of 29.7% compared with the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions mainly arise from the greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the consumption of electricity generated by fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO₂e per person, a decrease of 45.2% compared with 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the HKMA has also adopted digital tools and technologies, and automated and streamlined workflows, to build a digitalised working environment and enhance online collaboration within the organisation. Paperless meetings have become the HKMA's main mode of holding meetings. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, various internal administrative matters are primarily handled through electronic processes. In addition, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digitalised working practices by replacing paper documents and communications with digital means. At the same time, work to implement an electronic recordkeeping system is also in progress. The above green and digitalisation measures have brought about positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kilograms per person, a significant decrease of 64.8% compared with 2015 (Figure 3). As most international events have resumed being held in physical format following the COVID-19 pandemic, and as it is also necessary to promote the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, it is inevitable that certain HKMA staff need to travel abroad on business. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff, where feasible, to take direct flights or combine multiple business trips into one when participating in overseas activities. At the organisational level, in 2023 the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO₂e through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA participated in a "Gold Standard"-certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the programme carries out waste-to-energy projects, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement processes take into account sustainability and environmental considerations. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation's procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been formalised, and follows the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. In addition, the tender evaluation criteria now also incorporate ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency. At the same time, all suppliers are required to commit to complying with environmental regulations. Following the "4R" principles, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, the HKMA has adopted a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The breakdown of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfill and various types of recyclable waste, is set out in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA directly participated for the first time in the red packet recycling programme of the management company of the International Finance Centre office building. Staff handed in a total of about 3,000 used but still pristine red packets. These red packets were subsequently passed to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use in the coming Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operational and back-up data centres account for a major part of the organisation's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE). In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres were awarded "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the 2021 assessment guidelines "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres"; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The 2023 Data include the total energy consumption in 2023, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), their respective densities, and the changes in these data compared with the 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data also include the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the changes compared with the level when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, and also covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (except for the amount of food waste). The scope of verification covered a total of 5 office and warehouse assets, of which 4 offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is located at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed the representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 5 assets. This verification was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information", issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion so as to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was completely independent and impartial. The verification team of the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency was not involved in the preparation process of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data are materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threats posed by climate change are imminent, making it urgent to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record, and also the first year in which the global temperature exceeded pre-industrial levels by the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius. At the same time, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased somewhat during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current measures to mitigate climate change. In the process of addressing global warming, the materialization of climate-related risks is set to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Moreover, the current tense geopolitical situation, the increasing fragmentation of the global economic landscape, the feared aggravation of energy security concerns, coupled with an uncertain economic outlook, all pose greater challenges for countries in tackling climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Across the globe, Asia in particular faces the most severe transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum has pointed out, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth, but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a critical role in whether the world can smoothly achieve the goal of net-zero emissions. As a leading international financial centre in Asia, Hong Kong needs to strengthen its leading role and fully harness the power of finance to support and drive the transition within the region. To this end, the HKMA last year unveiled the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda," setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating the concept of sustainable development into the core of the financial system. On the one hand, our work focuses on enhancing the financial industry's capacity to address climate-related risks, and on the other hand, it focuses on helping the industry seize the relevant new opportunities. At the same time, we also lead by example and play a guiding role. The HKMA's sustainable development work encompasses four major areas: supporting the banking sector in moving towards net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and driving more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a critical role in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and Asia, but during the transition process it also faces considerable risks itself. In the "Action Agenda," we set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and to achieve net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. At the same time, we require all banks to strengthen the disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks' climate risk management, we also provide guidance for banks' transition planning to help them enhance their capacity to cope with the transition and better manage the relevant risks. We are also carrying out preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with the aim of further enhancing the industry's transparency in relevant activities. In addition, we are refining the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year to include more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We hope that by providing clear criteria, we can guide more funds towards sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks that may affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investment projects. But at the same time, it also brings opportunities for the Exchange Fund to grow and drive positive impacts. Our experience has proven that investment returns and positive sustainable impacts can be harmonized with each other, with no conflict between the two. In light of this, we are committed to striving to achieve net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and in the "Action Agenda" we have pledged to support Asia's climate transition through the Exchange Fund's investments. Currently, sustainable investments already account for more than ten per cent of the "Investment Portfolio." To further promote sustainable investment within the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships in November last year with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation, to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in the Asian region through co-investment. In addition, in September last year we published the first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise asset ownership and adopt good sustainable investment practices. Financing is particularly important for accelerating the transition within the region. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers (including mainland provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays an important role in channelling funds to accelerate the transition within the region. The "Action Agenda" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region, as well as the goal of fostering innovation in sustainable finance. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive green bond innovation (including the issuance of the world's first batch of multi-currency digital bonds in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" in May last year to cover transition financing instruments, and to the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" launched in November last year, we have been committed to encouraging issuers in the region to use Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the funds needed for the transition to decarbonization. To achieve a robust transition, in addition to capital and innovation, it also requires the support of an inclusive and easily accessible sustainable development system. This includes reliable sustainable development data, highly transparent information disclosure, and industry talent equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, in the "Action Agenda" we have pledged to support the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosure, as well as to strive to fill the gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge within the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosure, particularly by providing a convenient and easy-to-use climate disclosure template to facilitate sustainability disclosure by SMEs. We also launched the "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional-level module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking in November last year, to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. In addition, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we enabled people from all sectors to participate in discussions on sustainable development, thereby fostering cooperation and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with our vision for sustainable development. In the "Action Agenda," we have pledged to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or earlier, which is 20 years ahead of our original commitment. In addition, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap promulgated by the Government. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low-carbon emissions as a screening factor in the procurement process. At the same time, we continue to improve work efficiency through digitalization, cultivate a culture of sustainable development within the organization, and motivate staff to actively participate in sustainable development work. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic shifts in geopolitics have added uncertainties to global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an indisputable fact, and it is gradually intensifying. In the work of addressing climate change, the current situation does not allow us to relax in the slightest. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help reduce the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system, and in the process bring us opportunities. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, striving to advance our sustainable development work and deepen our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the severe challenges we face, we will, as always, remain committed to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the current generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub within Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and around the world. In October 2024, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), which sets out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving various goals, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance the relevant efforts. Through formulating strategic policies, strengthening supervisory engagement, and enhancing internal operations, the HKMA plans to reinforce the ability of Hong Kong's financial industry and the HKMA itself to address climate change risks, and to promote the Asian region's transition to a more sustainable economy. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the HKMA is also committed to exerting its influence and taking part in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking industry, as well as supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the transition to net-zero emissions. Our priorities for 2025 include: - Launching a new round of thematic examinations on banks' climate risk management practices, and conducting a third round of consultation meetings, to review banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant supervisory requirements and to further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - Refining the work of incorporating climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's supervisory-driven stress testing framework; - Continuing to advance the work of integrating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; - Commencing preparatory work on formulating relevant supervisory requirements for the local banking industry to implement the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - Completing the preparation of a new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual, providing guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to being a banking regulator, the HKMA also plays the role of a facilitator, committed to promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for the transition. We have published the first phase of the "Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance", providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitating the relevant financing. The HKMA has commenced work on the second phase of the taxonomy to expand its coverage, including adding transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate change adaptation objectives. In addition, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will hold another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks' adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well positioned to support the region's sustainable financing needs. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme", whose expanded coverage will include sustainable projects, such as socially responsible projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a demonstration for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable funds. We will also strengthen our promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions and enterprises from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing subsidies to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme". Although market demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures by institutions and enterprises is increasing, different entities vary in their capabilities and levels of preparedness in making sustainable disclosures, and some entities may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to work with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainable disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with a richer set of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainable disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how to leverage technology to further make existing resources more accessible and easy to use; and work with major local industry organisations to provide the training needed by the industry. The sustainable finance market is rapidly changing, requiring the expansion of the local talent pool and the closing of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key work in 2025 includes collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training courses for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners", as well as identifying areas where the industry has further training needs through the forthcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study. In addition, we plan to work with key stakeholders to strengthen the promotion of the government-funded "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme" and to review the scheme's scope of applicability. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks" to launch dedicated programmes in the Asian region, including conducting green finance research, providing insightful market analysis, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps to make green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or before, in support of the overall economic transition. Through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, we will continuously enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in institutional sustainability efforts. In line with the timeline for accelerating the achievement of net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Agenda", the HKMA will progressively incorporate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment and reporting at a pragmatic pace, and continue to advance the institution's sustainable development. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on the material issues. In addition, we will conduct energy audits and use technology solutions to assess the significant impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, in order to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the "Hong Kong Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure" published by the Government, and are actively undertaking preparatory work to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects in accordance with energy efficiency and energy conservation principles. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainable development and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and improving the overall digital experience for our staff, banks and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to reducing its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, a banking regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor, and a sustainable development organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of relevant strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of relevant measures; and ensure that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working methods. In its commitment to sound corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for sustainability-related work, featuring clear accountability arrangements and a high level of transparency. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainability efforts. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for monitoring the HKMA's work, including its sustainability efforts, and making recommendations; - The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA's Chief Executive, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; - In the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - For other functional areas, the relevant teams and working groups, which are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), jointly initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability efforts over the past years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas. The Steering Committee is responsible for: - Providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across four functional areas, namely banking, the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; - Overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; - Assessing the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - Overseeing the external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the HKMA's Chief Executive, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. In addition, we invite the Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions relevant to green and sustainability matters to attend the Steering Committee meetings to report on the major achievements of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee holds meetings regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's banking-related departments, the Corporate Development and Operations Department, the External Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA — together with the SFC — jointly initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts on the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, in order to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system in coping with climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. In their day-to-day business operations, banks are exposed to the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters, and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by channelling funds towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), setting out the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a sustainable finance hub in the region and to support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The "Action Agenda" comprises eight major goals across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the goals of the relevant banking policies, we have been carrying out the following work. All banks strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero emissions in their financing by 2050 or earlier; all banks increase the transparency of climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices in transition planning with the industry, and launched an industry consultation on the draft module GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to respond to the net-zero transition and on the related risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating into the assessment process the relevant factors put forward by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (the Basel Committee) on the effective management of climate-related financial risks, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risks. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "Action Agenda". In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (the Taxonomy) to address the industry's concerns about greenwashing and to help channel funds towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, and aims to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating relevant elements to reflect local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope covered by the Taxonomy, and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable funds. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management, and was committed to supporting banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all the work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risks into the banking supervisory process. To promote banks' capacity to strengthen climate risk management, the HKMA shared with the banking industry the good practices observed during thematic examinations and consultation sessions, which mainly include: - establishing a robust governance structure that clearly sets out the responsibilities of the board and senior management; - ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters, namely (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and execution of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a roundtable meeting on balanced supervision, with a focus on the theme of climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on a range of climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, and transition planning and financing. This roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and helped inform the HKMA's work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA launched a round of thematic examinations on banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, and assessed their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The thematic examinations covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held a second series of consultation sessions to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual, and to understand the challenges they faced. The consultation sessions also covered the latest supervisory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance based on the specific circumstances of individual banks to support their climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of the banking sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) in 2024, with a total of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups participating. The results showed that, under various scenarios (including those assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and a macroeconomic downturn), the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience in withstanding severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, the participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. The HKMA understands that banks face numerous challenges relating to data and methodologies in climate risk management, and has therefore been committed to a number of initiatives to promote the application of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for conducting climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched the Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform in response to user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA collaborated with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the financial services industry as a whole. During the year, we published an implementation practice guide and two "Regtech Use Case Reports" (in English), setting out technology solutions used for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as for greenwashing risk management. We also held the third "FiNETech" event, bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. The HKMA is keenly aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing monitoring work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its continuous monitoring of financial stability risks, and has incorporated analysis of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helped further enrich climate scenarios, assisting central banks and supervisors in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth edition of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analysing the interaction between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the "Practical Guide for the Application of Green Technology by Banks" (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the economy as a whole. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in withstanding monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial industry in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The findings of the above research not only deepened our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, helping to inform the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, this research helped strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings were also shared with a wide range of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the HKMA Research Memoranda. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (the Research Centre), which is responsible for research work under the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provided evidence that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing, and highlighted its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the Research Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research" and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, we help promote international and regional policy dialogue on responding to climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw on the insights gained to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA's "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), the HKMA is dedicated to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of financial markets, enhancing sustainability disclosures by the industry, expanding the local pool of green talent, and addressing the knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region.  Developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally; catalysing sustainable finance innovation; supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures; bridging the talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region.  To demonstrate the Government's determination to respond to climate change, promote green finance and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling around USD 28 billion equivalent, sold to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including the currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the Programme and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the Programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects, and it was renamed the Government Sustainable Bond Programme (the Sustainable Bond Programme).  To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report, which details the allocation of the proceeds raised from the green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing around USD 3 billion equivalent of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This tri-currency issuance covered bonds of different tenors denominated in renminbi, US dollars and euros. These bonds attracted the participation of various types of investors and received an enthusiastic subscription response, recording subscriptions of over USD 15 billion equivalent. Among them, the 20-year and 30-year renminbi green bonds were issued by the Government for the first time and represented the longest-tenor renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date, providing a new benchmark for the market and further reinforcing the demonstrative role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the choice of offshore renminbi investment products in Hong Kong. In addition, the enthusiastic response of global investors to the green bonds issued by the Government reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development.  To encourage more borrowers in the region to raise sustainable development funds through Hong Kong's financing platform, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme launched in May 2021, which provides subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The Scheme has been widely welcomed by the industry. As at the end of 2024, the Scheme had approved subsidies for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total amount of over USD 140 billion. The Scheme was extended for three years to 2027 in May 2024, with its scope of subsidy expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the Scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to make use of Hong Kong's transition financing platform to progressively reduce carbon emissions.  - Approved subsidies for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total amount of over USD 140 billion (as at the end of 2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, with the scope of subsidy expanded to cover transition financing instruments  At the same time, the HKMA has actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, and this work has yielded encouraging results. Among these, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time in August, totalling RMB 7 billion, including RMB 2.7 billion of green bonds, RMB 1 billion of sustainable bonds and RMB 900 million of social responsibility bonds. In September, the People's Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion of green bonds. In October, the People's Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB 3 billion, including RMB 1 billion of blue bonds and RMB 1 billion of sustainable bonds. The above bond issuance activities once again highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable funds between the Mainland and the rest of the world.  Through the above measures, Hong Kong has been able to consolidate its position as the preferred sustainable financing platform in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in Asia in 2024, with the total amount of relevant bonds arranged in Hong Kong reaching USD 43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total.  To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark batches of tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, being the world's first tokenised government green bond and the world's first multi-currency digital bond respectively. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for the adoption of asset digitalisation and innovative technologies by market participants in the green and sustainable finance space in the region. In November, the HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting the innovative development of Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market.  The Working Group on Sustainability Disclosures under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group) has been making efforts on Hong Kong's adoption of the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (the ISSB Standards). In December 2024, the Government published the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong, providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to provide support for entities at different stages of preparedness to achieve high-quality sustainability disclosures, making sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive.  It is worth mentioning that we continued to encourage the use of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies (the Questionnaire), which was jointly launched by the Steering Group and CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainability disclosures by enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to enable enterprises to fill it in online (see the QR code below). The HKMA is enhancing the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly. Specific measures include selecting core questions from the Questionnaire and providing common use scenarios for the Questionnaire. In addition, we also strive to improve the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage.  The HKMA leads by example, making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content, including the HKMA's climate-related risks in its operations as an organisation, as well as its plans and implementation progress towards achieving its climate targets. For details of the sustainability disclosures on our own operations, please refer to the chapter "A Sustainable HKMA".  In view of the rapidly changing sustainable finance market, and to bridge the knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is stepping up its skills training efforts in the banking industry, as well as fostering knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, together with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the Foundation level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework (ECF) for banking practitioners in July 2023. The module aims to help banking professionals acquire knowledge and develop professional competencies in green and sustainable finance in a more effective manner, and covers four main areas of work: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainable/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosures and reporting; and (4) sustainable strategy, compliance and controls. In addition, the Professional level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, targeting middle and senior banking practitioners responsible for the relevant work, was also launched in November.  To provide the necessary training for banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the administering body of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the Foundation level training course of the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking industry in 2025 to develop the Professional level training course. To understand the further skills and training needs of the banking industry, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking industry to conduct the study "Future Banking Talent for 2026 to 2030", with the goal of publishing the study findings in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the "Future Banking Talent for 2021 to 2025" paper published in June 2020. The findings of the follow-up study will provide an important reference for the industry, helping it to formulate and adjust its talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking industry.  Through its collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continued to assist in implementing the government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which subsidises practitioners, graduates and students to undertake sustainable finance-related training. As at December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses had been registered as eligible training courses under the Scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025-26 Budget that the Scheme would be extended to 2028.  The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international collaboration. As a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions centring on the global sustainable finance market, policy frameworks and innovative tools. In addition, the HKMA supported the establishment of a chapter of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training efforts relating to transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively takes the lead in advancing the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA upholds the philosophy of responsible investment in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritising sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value creation", the HKMA believes that giving due regard to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate the relevant investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a firm signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment work. We attach particular importance to sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and striving for more favourable risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to channel capital towards sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA released the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to investment partners through the annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practices and standards, and to promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and the central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), setting out the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future.  The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The foremost guiding principle sets the tone that the HKMA, in practising responsible investment, is able to take into account the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund at the same time. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors the relevant implementation progress through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investing Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As illustrated in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategist, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and joined by the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Strategist of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures across the HKMA's various functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in pursuit of the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investing Team works closely with the various teams of the Exchange Fund Investment Office on the integration of ESG factors, and assists the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG, and in particular climate-related, risks and opportunities across different types of investments:  - Public market investments — The Credit, Regulatory and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior members of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the situation after ESG factors have been integrated into the credit risk model with reference to the views of the Sustainable Investing Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting from the Risk Management and Compliance Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investing Team also participates in the selection, appointment and monitoring processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (for details, please refer to the section "Promoting Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" under the "Risk Management" section on page 39).  - Private market investments — The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams on each investment proposal.  The HKMA understands that the physical and transition risks brought about by climate change, as well as the associated opportunities, will affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund's investments. The Emissions Gap Report 2024 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless there is a large-scale global mobilisation to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, global average temperatures will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. The uncertainties surrounding policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may intensify transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the growing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries towards sustainable solutions also creates potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future is aligned with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050, and continues to advance its work through an orderly three-pronged approach to achieve this goal (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the "Action Agenda", which consolidated the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts relating to the climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA is inclined to proactively engage rather than to exclude or divest from investable assets.  Investing in a Sustainable Future The Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 - Actively expanding the scope and variety of sustainable investments, especially climate-transition-themed investments in the public and private markets - Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with particular attention to climate change and transition prospects considerations - Formulating clear ESG expectations that are in line with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to comply with them - Committing to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by 2030  Supporting the Regional Transition through Investment - Continuing to engage with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that drive the transition - Continuing to identify and prioritise quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia's transition and bring positive impact to the world  First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA is able to seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition and that possess superior technology and sound corporate governance to respond to the ever-changing global climate trends, including companies in high-emitting industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding the relevant investments or divesting does not help resolve the issue of carbon emissions. On the contrary, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, driving them to transition towards sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about favourable changes both for themselves and for the world at large. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, so as to drive comprehensive decarbonisation across the entire economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of an asset portfolio depends not only on the portfolio's own adjustments, but also on a broad-based economic transition. Although there is no perfect single solution, the HKMA enhanced its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive the transition while supporting the net-zero goals of both the Exchange Fund and the world. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors into fundamental analysis and stewardship, portfolio decarbonisation tilting, and thematic investments in various assets that are aligned with the pathway towards net-zero emissions. In the public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In the private markets, there may be a greater focus on transition-enabling investments. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can facilitate the climate transition while also enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio.  Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio", with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5).  - Public market investments — The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and the climate transition, and expanded the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continued to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide competitive returns while funding sustainable projects (for a relevant case study, see the section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds").  - Private market investments — The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes.
