The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. In 2024, one of its key priorities in delivering on this commitment was the plan to bring forward its target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030—20 years ahead of the original target—in line with the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda". In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to advancing staff training and well-being, and to promoting financial inclusion as well as enhancing the public's financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for the various corporate sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 the HKMA's new target of achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations by 2030, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" ("Action Agenda"). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability initiatives relating to corporate operations, staff well-being, and social connectedness, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on corporate sustainability initiatives. The Green Office Theme Group and the Volunteer Service Group, made up of staff from various operational departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and putting forward suggestions on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its staff, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 18 consecutive years, from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to adopt a structure comprising three pillars: environmental, staff, and social responsibility.  - Focusing on decarbonisation and digitalisation of the HKMA's day-to-day operations, with a target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 - Adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promoting greener operational practices to the financial industry and the wider community - Building a proactive workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Creating a working environment that fosters collaboration and a caring and inclusive culture, values diversity, and strengthens staff's sense of belonging - Providing a quality working environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Cultivating a culture of care for society - Incorporating social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promoting financial inclusion and enhancing the public's financial literacy through consumer education activities  The HKMA is attentive to climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its own corporate operations to 2030—20 years ahead of its original commitment—as part of the "Action Agenda". The HKMA has revised its roadmap for the transition to net zero, with a focus on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its day-to-day operations, concentrating on reducing carbon emissions, saving energy and paper, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging the improvements made by local power companies in their fuel mix for electricity generation. In addition, the HKMA is building a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, the HKMA recognises the importance of cultivating a culture of sustainability, and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt sustainability-friendly practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the overriding 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and to procure with low carbon wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023 the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel and participation in a carbon offset programme. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and carbon offset programmes to cover all remaining major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to actual operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, ranging from the introduction of electronic document submission and processing procedures to the promotion of electronic payments and the recirculation of coins back into the market. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as in promoting staff well-being and caring for society.  Under the HKMA's overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing the potential risks and threats—including those arising from climate change—that the HKMA faces in its day-to-day operations. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the design of the HKMA's offices incorporates a range of measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire, and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only the offices but also communications and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring the transition risks it faces by tracking the greenhouse gas emissions generated by its own operations, waste generation, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 relating to its corporate operations by 2030. These targets were set with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA adopts the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's principal greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of fossil fuels to generate electricity. As no supplier-specific data is available, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach in estimating the principal Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfill and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria of its verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" attached at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, upholding the same climate-related standards that it expects of the banks it regulates and the financial system it supervises.  As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024, and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve full green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in the various renovation works carried out in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fit-out materials, or traded in old items for a discount on new ones, to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews the energy consumption and energy-saving measures of its offices and data centre, and in 2024 adopted a modular-design uninterruptible power supply system in its data centre facility upgrade project, further optimising the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency under partial load, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. Through the digital workplace, the HKMA has enhanced internal virtual collaboration and, together with streamlined workflows, has effectively reduced paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of its mobile and desktop devices with reference to manufacturers' software update cycles, thereby prolonging the secure usable life of the devices. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the "4R" principles—refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has recycling bins at various convenient locations in its offices to recycle different materials. To improve the recycling rate, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit netting in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending the food waste it collects to a waste-to-energy centre in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department's "Waste Reduction Pledge for Events", pledging to take measures to reduce the waste generated by its various events. The HKMA continues to give priority to procuring goods that meet the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their itineraries carefully, for example by combining multiple trips as far as possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing carbon emissions from annual air travel by about 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in a "Gold Standard"-certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the programme focuses on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged a number of learning activities for staff, such as talks and guided tour services of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance staff's understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the whole of May, the HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month", themed "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This was a good opportunity for the HKMA to advance its commitment and momentum in putting environmental sustainability into practice in its internal operations. The activities included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" encouraging staff to practise green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and a Japanese-inspired "kokedama" indoor plant care workshop; waste audit results were also shared, and a community recycling centre operator introduced best practices in recycling. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month", the HKMA launched a recycling campaign lasting about six months in October, highlighting the responsible handling of waste and reminding staff that pooling together small changes in individual habits can greatly enhance the organisation's overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of a "Green Action" video, in which several senior executives shared recycling tips. The campaign also rolled out a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders to remind staff to reduce waste and increase recycling in practice. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff questionnaire survey to understand their awareness of sustainability and to gather their views on the proposed green office measures. The survey results will help shape future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency ("HKQAA") conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Data includes the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel for 2024, together with their respective intensities. In addition, the Data includes Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions arising from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered a total of six office and warehouse assets, of which five offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, while the warehouse is located at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance of the accuracy and reliability of the Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the six assets. This verification was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and draw conclusions so as to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was established in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed and tested the reliability of the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - The Data is substantially accurate and reliable; - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate.
